{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Vendor: Brightline)
**Privileged and confidential — attorney work product**

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our contracting playbook. The agreement is, on the whole, strongly favourable to us: the critical protections on indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit (§ 22), governing law (§ 28) and insurance (§ 18) all meet or exceed our preferred positions. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, minimum-commitment or customer-side MFN burden on us, and renewal mechanics are within tolerance.

Two issues require redlines:

1. **Limitation of liability cap basis (§ 21, critical).** The carve-outs and mutuality are correct, but "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee in the first Order Form, making the aggregate cap effectively USD 12,000 — an illusory cap. We are changing the basis to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding 12 months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor; our fallback is a straight 12-month amounts cap.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7, high).** Late payment triggers liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay. Our playbook prohibits Customer-payable liquidated damages, and this figure is punitive — it would rapidly exceed remaining contract value and sits uneasily with the dispute-withholding right in § 7.3 and the § 21.1 cap (which does not limit Fee obligations). We are striking it and substituting ordinary late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy.

We note for completeness that the indemnity is uncapped because § 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as an Excluded Claim, so the cap-base defect does not impair our indemnity recovery.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

## Walk-away items

- **§ 7.7 liquidated damages.** The 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week late payment penalty is in walk-away territory. We need this deleted and replaced with ordinary late-payment interest as Vendor's sole remedy for late payment.

No other walk-away trigger is engaged. In particular, the three-year duration in § 8.1 is the initial term of the master agreement, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so the renewal walk-away trigger does not apply.

## Next steps

1. **Issue redlines on the two deviations:** (a) § 21 — replace the "Fees"/first Order Form cap basis with the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000, holding the § 21.3 Excluded Claims intact; and (b) § 7.7 — delete the Customer-payable liquidated damages and substitute ordinary late-payment interest.
2. **Confirm the fallback authority** on the cap: a straight 12-month amounts-paid-or-payable cap without the USD 1,000,000 floor, if Vendor resists the floor.
3. **Sanity-check the definitions.** Ensure the amended § 21 cap language does not rely on the defined term "Fees" (defined by reference to the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee), and that the § 7.3 dispute-withholding right is preserved alongside the revised late-payment remedy.
4. **Accept the balance of the agreement as drafted**, subject to commercial sign-off; no further legal redlines are required on the compliant items above."}
